papers.title: EEG2MCU: Sensing-to-Execution Co-Design for Wearable EEG Inference
papers.abstract: Wearable EEG inference is constrained not only by model size, but also by the channel-dependent sensing front end that must process high-dimensional inputs before compact downstream computation. We present EEG2MCU, a sensing-to-execution co-design framework that treats electrode count as a hardware design variable through task-aware montage selection. EEG2MCU retains a compact time-frequency representation and generates only the INT8 regions required by each first-layer tile, avoiding full input materialization. Halo reuse and access-aware placement across Flash, SRAM, and tightly coupled memory further reduce redundant generation and data movement. On a Cortex-M7 MCU, EEG2MCU reduces peak SRAM by 11.38x relative to the baseline, including a 1.71x reduction from the 62-to-19 electrode montage, while reducing latency by 2.57x and energy by 2.48x. It retains 94-96% of full-montage accuracy, demonstrating practical high-dimensional EEG inference under tight embedded-resource constraints.

papers.title: LogicSleep: a neurosymbolic-guided framework for explainable and personalized sleep staging.
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is important for diagnosing and managing sleep disorders. However, artificial intelligence-based models still struggle with explainability, sequence plausibility, and personalization across subjects. We propose LogicSleep, a neurosymbolic framework that integrates transition rules with deep learning models for explainable, physiologically valid, and subject-adaptive sleep staging. LogicSleep extracts multi-level evidence from raw polysomnography via a CNN-graph U-Net backbone, providing explainable patterns beyond classification. Sequence plausibility is enforced by combining Conditional Random Fields with Deep Learning with Differentiable Logics (DL2) rules, which discourage implausible transitions, promote physiologically valid ones, and regularize dwell times; the same rules also guide subject-specific test-time adaptation via entropy minimization. Across different datasets (i.e., ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3 datasets), under both within- and cross-dataset settings, LogicSleep consistently outperforms strong baselines and improves sequence-level metrics. Ablations confirm complementary contributions of each component. LogicSleep advances sleep staging toward physiologically plausible, personalized, and explainable predictions.

ai.reason: Directly on sleep staging with explainability, cross-dataset evaluation, and subject-specific adaptation—core priorities, though the CNN-graph U-Net backbone implies heavier compute.
ai.summary: LogicSleep is a neurosymbolic framework combining a CNN-graph U-Net backbone with Conditional Random Fields and differentiable-logic transition rules to produce physiologically valid, subject-adaptive sleep staging. It outperformed strong baselines on ISRUC_S1, ISRUC_S3, and MASS_SS3, including under cross-dataset settings, and improved sequence-level metrics and explainability.

papers.title: Reference Coordinates, Output Perturbations, and Information Loss in EEG Decoding
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoders can respond to reference changes that preserve all relative-potential information. We use established measurement-operator theory to distinguish coordinate sensitivity, additional output-channel perturbations, and electrode loss. Exact pseudoinverse alignment supplies a consistency control; measurement-operator canonicalization (MOC) denotes a graph-Tikhonov estimator. The broader evaluation covers three public motor-imagery datasets and four decoders. The primary EEGNet comparison on Cho2017 and PhysioNet uses three paired training seeds, three shared noise realizations, and six front ends, with identical CAR training inputs sharing checkpoints. At 10 dB output perturbation, MOC-minus-raw disagreement was -0.144 and -0.107, while balanced-accuracy differences were 0.044 and 0.050, respectively; these four contrasts passed the retained Holm correction. MOC also reduced disagreement relative to pseudoinversion across all three seeds in both cohorts. However, comparison with fixed graph smoothing after pseudoinversion did not establish an additional MOC benefit. Preserving zero reference rows changed raw disagreement by less than 0.001 in magnitude; inverse-method predictions were unchanged. For canonical front ends, cross-reference disagreement was close to the reference obtained from independent noise within the same operator. Controlled weak-mode reconstruction and equal-rank electrode masks exposed separate stability and information-loss effects. The results locate the complete-reference gains within spatial processing under the specified stress model, while requiring decoding accuracy alongside consistency to assess practical utility.

Measurement-operator canonicalization (MOC) reduced reference disagreement and improved balanced accuracy versus raw processing at 10 dB output perturbation, though no additional benefit over fixed graph smoothing after pseudoinversion was established, and accuracy alongside consistency was required to assess utility.

papers.title: Exploratory evaluation of electroencephalogram-derived features for classification of mild cognitive impairment in two independent datasets.
papers.abstract: A proper diagnosis of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is one of the important challenges in the early detection of dementia. For the classification of MCI patients and healthy controls, some electroencephalogram (EEG)-derived indices were calculated and compared. Some studies have been conducted on the high accuracy classification of MCI patients and healthy controls, but classification may depend on the dataset and recording conditions. In this study, we evaluated EEG-derived indices in the Japanese and the Iranian EEG datasets and examined their classification performance under within-dataset and cross-dataset validation. This classifier had common features but was learned for each dataset. The Japanese dataset consisted of 7 MCI patients and 10 healthy controls. The Iranian dataset consisted of 29 MCI patients and 32 healthy controls. The common 16 EEG data were separated into 5 frequency bands. Power spectrum and SL values by Synchronization Likelihood were calculated as features for classification. These standardized and exponentially transformed indices were also used as features. Furthermore, graph metrics were calculated based on SL values before or after standardization and exponential transformation. Features used for classification were selected from these indices. The high classification accuracies were obtained from the classifier using a 34-dimensional feature subset selected from standardized and exponentially transformed EEG-derived indices for lower alpha band. Accuracies of this classifier were 88.24% in the Japanese dataset and 86.89% in the Iranian dataset. To evaluate classification accuracy while minimizing information leakage and optimistic bias, nested leave-one-out cross-validation was performed. Accuracies were 88.24% in the Japanese dataset and 83.61% in the Iranian dataset using exponentially transformed EEG-derived indices for lower alpha band. To evaluate whether the classifier can generalize to independent datasets obtained under different recording conditions, exploratory bidirectional cross-dataset evaluation was performed. Accuracies were 40.98% (Training data: the Japanese dataset, Test data: the Iranian dataset) and 58.82% (Training data: the Iranian dataset, Test data: the Japanese dataset). These findings suggested that resting-state EEG-derived indices for lower alpha band may contain information useful for classification of MCI patients and healthy controls. However, they suggested that classifier based on these indices may partly reflect dataset-specific characteristics.

ai.reason: Directly tests within- vs cross-dataset validation of spectral/synchronization EEG features, relevant to signal normalization and generalizable pipelines; small clinical cohorts but methodologically transferable.
ai.summary: This exploratory study evaluated EEG-derived spectral, synchronization-likelihood, and graph-metric features for classifying mild cognitive impairment versus healthy controls in Japanese and Iranian datasets. Lower-alpha-band exponentially transformed features achieved nested cross-validated accuracies of 88.24% (Japanese) and 83.61% (Iranian), but bidirectional cross-dataset transfer dropped to 40.98% and 58.82%, indicating dataset-specific characteristics.

papers.title: Longitudinal resting-state EEG-based modeling predicts phenoconversion and delineates heterogeneity in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder.
papers.abstract: Isolated REM sleep behavior disorder is a high-risk prodromal syndrome for Lewy body diseases but highly heterogeneous. Neurophysiologic markers resolving this heterogeneity and predicting phenoconversion remain limited. We applied Subtype and Stage Inference (SuStaIn) modeling to longitudinal resting-state EEG from a prospective cohort of 285 participants. SuStaIn identified a progressive degenerative subtype (Subtype 2), characterized by delta/theta increases and lower MoCA scores, and a posterior beta-low subtype (Subtype 1), which was longitudinally unstable and of uncertain independent prognostic significance. Longitudinal validation demonstrated substantial subtype shifting in Subtype 1 and stage advancement predominantly in Subtype 2. In Kaplan-Meier analysis, subtype shifting and accelerated annual stage advancement (ΔStage≥2) identified individuals at exceptionally high phenoconversion risk with survival approaching 0-15% by 7.5 years. These findings extend SuStaIn beyond cross-sectional inference by incorporating longitudinal subtype-shifting and stage-advancement features to stratify prodromal heterogeneity and predict neurodegenerative progression.

A progressive degenerative subtype showed delta/theta increases and stage advancement, and subtype shifting or accelerated stage progression identified individuals with exceptionally high phenoconversion risk (survival 0–15% by 7.5 years).

papers.title: Small or large patches? History, biophysics, and an empirical test of a core assumption in EEG independent component analysis
papers.abstract: This is a methods paper on the physiological interpretation of independent component analysis (ICA) applied to scalp EEG, but its scope extends to historical review and hypothesis-driven research. First, we trace how the small-patch model, which equates each brain independent component (IC) with a cortical patch smaller than 1 cm square, became the central assumption of this interpretation. Second, we review a clinically and biophysically grounded alternative, the large-patch model (>= 6 cm square). The two models make opposing predictions: the small-patch model predicts that about two-thirds of ICs lie on sulcal walls with tangential dipoles, whereas the large-patch model predicts radial dipoles displaced deeper than the cortex because fitting a single dipole to an extended source produces depth bias. Third, we test them: in simulation, depth bias grew with patch radius and was modulated, but not eliminated, by skull-conductivity mismatch. In resting-state EEG from two open datasets (820 recordings; 14,578 qualified brain ICs), 77.6% of fitted dipoles lay more than 5 mm inward from the template boundary and 57.9% lay more than 14 mm inward. The pooled signed-distance distribution showed two prominent peaks, near -1 mm and -19 mm, separated by a pronounced minimum near -5 mm (2-mm bins). Fitted dipole orientations showed no tangential dominance among deep ICs, which also exhibited higher activation power and lower residual variance than superficial ICs. These results favor the large-patch model. ICA remains valid for separating EEG sources, but the depths of fitted dipoles may reflect the spatial extent of the underlying current sources.

ai.reason: Clarifies physiological interpretation of ICA components and dipole depth bias, relevant to artifact/component selection decisions in EEG preprocessing.
ai.summary: Contrasts the small-patch and large-patch models of EEG independent component dipole interpretation using simulations and resting-state EEG from 820 recordings (14,578 brain ICs). Found 77.6% of fitted dipoles lay >5 mm inward from the template boundary, dipole orientations showed no tangential dominance among deep ICs, and results favored the large-patch model, attributing fitted dipole depths to source spatial extent.

papers.title: Spectral and complexity-based signatures of advanced concentration absorption meditation: A high-density EEG study of jhana
papers.abstract: Advanced meditation provides structured and reproducible alterations of consciousness that are increasingly used as model states for the neuroscience of consciousness. Jhana-type advanced concentration absorption meditation (ACAM-J) consists of eight progressively deepening absorption states (ACAM-J1-8) in which sensory and self-referential content gradually attenuate. We applied high-density EEG and a comprehensive multidimensional battery of spectral and complexity measures to characterize each ACAM-J state individually in 20 advanced meditators, together with phenomenological ratings. ACAM-J produced widespread posterior-central reductions in oscillatory and aperiodic power, posterior aperiodic flattening across all eight states, and convergent increases in entropy-based complexity over the posterior cortex, with power effects strengthening with phenomenological depth. Crucially, neural complexity remained elevated even in the late, most minimal and unified states, in opposition to the prevailing account that links higher neural entropy to richer phenomenal content. Between practitioners, lower power and higher entropy accompanied more visual and auditory but less bodily content, a redistribution rather than an enrichment of experience; within practitioners, only reduced low-frequency power tracked wider attention and less narrative thought. ACAM-J thus emerges as a non-pharmacological model state at the high-complexity end of the spectrum of altered consciousness, and reveals a previously unquantified dissociation between neural complexity and experiential richness for specific ACAM-J states.

ai.reason: High-density EEG spectral and complexity battery applied to state changes; methods (aperiodic power, entropy) transfer to vigilance-state analysis, though meditation-specific and not lightweight.
ai.summary: High-density EEG with spectral and complexity measures was used to characterize eight progressively deepening jhana absorption meditation states in 20 advanced meditators alongside phenomenological ratings. The states showed widespread posterior-central power reductions, posterior aperiodic flattening, and elevated entropy-based complexity that persisted into the most minimal states, dissociating neural complexity from experiential richness.

papers.title: Effects of pharmacotherapy on quantitative electroencephalogram measures of sleepiness in obstructive sleep apnea.
papers.abstract: Recent studies of noradrenergic and antimuscarinic agents to treat obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) have been promising, but their impact on subjective and objective sleep quality and daytime sleepiness have shown inconsistent results. This study aimed to assess the effects of the noradrenergic agent reboxetine alone and in combination with the antimuscarinic oxybutynin on next-day objective sleepiness through quantitative analysis of wake electroencephalography (qEEG) during a Karolinska Drowsiness Test (KDT). This was a secondary analysis from a randomised trial of reboxetine alone and in combination with oxybutynin versus placebo in 16 participants with OSA. All participates have undergone a KDT in the evening prior to drug or placebo administration and sleep opportunity, and ∼1hr post-waking next morning. Mixed models were used to examine drug effects on qEEG outcomes. There was no significant main effect of treatment (Reboxetine vs placebo vs Reboxetine-Oxybutynin) on slow EEG frequencies or theta/alpha ratio during the morning KDT. There was a significant main effect of testing time (evening vs morning) with higher morning delta and theta EEG power during eyes open and the delta power during entire KDT (all p < 0.001) compared to the evening test. There was a significant main effect of electrode position (F3, C3, O1), on wake delta and theta EEG with both frequencies higher in frontal (F3) vs occipital regions (O1) (all p < 0.001). There were no interaction effects and no correlations between qEEG outcomes and morning subjective sleepiness. Reboxetine with and without oxybutynin did not increase neurophysiological markers of next-day morning sleepiness as measured by wake delta and theta EEG power. These findings support the potential safety profile of these agents in respect to next-day sleepiness in people with OSA.

ai.reason: Quantitative wake EEG spectral analysis (delta/theta, theta/alpha) in a sleep-related context; useful spectral methodology but focused on clinical drug effects rather than computational methods.
ai.summary: Secondary analysis of a randomized trial in 16 OSA participants testing reboxetine alone and with oxybutynin found no significant treatment effect on wake qEEG markers of next-day sleepiness (delta/theta power, theta/alpha ratio) during morning Karolinska Drowsiness Tests, supporting the agents' safety regarding daytime sleepiness. Morning delta and theta power were higher than evening, with frontal predominance, and qEEG did not correlate with subjective sleepiness.

papers.title: Aberrant Interregional Brain Connectivity During Different Memory Processes in a Mouse Model of Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.abstract: Reduced working memory is a hallmark of Alzheimer's disease (AD). Analyzing local field potentials (LFPs) across neural networks provides crucial insights into the mechanisms underlying these cognitive deficits. Standard LFP studies often rely on spontaneous exploration, while we designed a novel Y-maze paradigm with aversive voltage feedback. This paradigm enable precise time-locked temporal subdivision of trials (first choice vs. second choice, correct vs. incorrect decisionst) to compare memory-related electrophysiology between AD and normal mice. Our analysis reveals four key findings: (1) LFP exhibit task-specific lateralization, suggesting the right hemisphere is prominently engaged during this specific spatial navigation context; (2) correct behavioral outcomes correlate with pre-decision neural states, highlighting distinct network encoding mechanisms compared to error processing; (3) causal connectivity suggests a disrupted functional balance between the cingulate gyrus and hippocampus in AD mice, it may reflect early network compensation; (4) AD mice display widespread oscillatory and directional connectivity disruptions during memory process, which strongly correlate with spatial memory failures. These findings characterize AD memory impairment as a dynamic network disconnectivity syndrome and highlight cingulate gyrus-hippocampal interactions as potential biomarkers to improve memory dysfunction in AD.

Causal connectivity analyses indicated a disrupted functional balance between cingulate gyrus and hippocampus in AD mice, proposed as early network compensation.

papers.title: Comparison of Infradian and Circadian Rhythms in Laboratory Rodents.
papers.abstract: Infradian cycles are multi-day oscillations whose mechanisms are still poorly understood, while circadian rhythms have been extensively studied and are well-documented in mammals. In this study, we monitored the locomotor activity of three rodent species: CD-1 mice (Mus musculus), Mongolian gerbils (Meriones unguiculatus), and white-tailed antelope squirrels (Ammospermophilus leucurus). We used Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis to verify the prevalence of circadian and infradian rhythms, the magnitude of the spectral power, and associations across species, rhythms, and sexes. Circadian rhythms were robust and were found for all animals. For infradian rhythms, the prevalence in mice was extremely low, whereas the prevalence in gerbils and squirrels was moderate in the 5- and 10-day ranges. In all cases, the strength of infradian rhythmicity was less than 10% of the strength of circadian rhythmicity. As no natural environmental cycle is documented to operate in the 5- to 10-day range, further studies are needed to determine whether an endogenous source may account for this weak but significant infradian rhythmicity.

papers.title: A mathematical programming approach for the robust resolution of superpositions of action potentials.
papers.abstract: Resolving the superposition of action potentials in neural recordings is essential for precise spike sorting, a key step in decoding neural activity. This study presents a novel mathematical programming approach to address this challenge. Our objective is to improve the accuracy and efficiency of superposition resolution by reformulating the problem as a quadratic mixed-integer programming problem. We developed a new framework that flexibly incorporates physiological constraints and adapts to various types of recordings. We validated our method using both simulated and experimental intramuscular electromyographic and neural signals. The performance was evaluated against the branch-and-bound algorithm, a leading method for resolving superpositions, focusing on accuracy and computational speed. We also tested its ability to handle complex cases, such as multiple occurrences of the same action potential, and leveraged multi-channel recordings to maintain high accuracy when some of the action potentials were unknown to the solver. Our approach successfully resolved superpositions of up to 15 action potentials with an accuracy exceeding 97%. It uniquely handles complex cases where the same action potential discharges multiple times, achieving 95% accuracy even with up to six repeated discharges of five distinct action potentials. Using 32-channel recordings, we maintained an identification rate of 94.6% for superpositions of five action potentials, even when 80% of the action potentials in the superpositions were unknown, demonstrating the framework's robustness to unknown action potentials interference. The proposed mathematical programming approach significantly improves the accuracy and efficiency of superposition resolution, especially in complex and challenging scenarios. This methodology offers a robust and flexible tool that can advance neural signal processing and our understanding of neural dynamics.

papers.title: Children become accurate years before they become fast: electroencephalography dates the separate maturation of decision components
papers.abstract: Perceptual decisions, a hallmark of cognitive development, become faster and more accurate from early childhood to adulthood, but whether the underlying components mature together, as a single global gain in processing speed would predict, or on separate timetables remains unclear. Behaviour alone cannot distinguish whether age-related improvement reflects clearer sensory encoding, more efficient evidence accumulation, fewer attention lapses or shorter non-decision processes, and prior direct measurements have typically come from small samples spanning limited age ranges. We analysed electroencephalography from 1,534 participants aged 5 to 21 years in the Healthy Brain Network during a contrast-change discrimination task. On the same trials, we measured the visual response and an evidence-accumulation signal, while a decision model estimated accumulation efficiency, attention lapses and non-decision time. We found that the visual response did not grow with age and retained 77% of its strength on missed targets. Instead, accuracy improved through fewer lapses and more efficient accumulation, both reaching half of their developmental change by about 9 years, whereas speed improved later: non-decision time shortened between 11 and 14 years and was longer in children whose accumulation signal rose later. These findings show that perceptual decision-making matures through dissociable stages rather than a single global increase in processing speed: mechanisms supporting accuracy mature in middle childhood, whereas those supporting the fastest responses continue to develop into early adolescence. This framework links developmental theories of processing speed to neural mechanisms of decision-making and provides a reference for identifying which component is disrupted in children who struggle.

ai.summary: Analyzing EEG from 1,534 participants aged 5-21 during a contrast-change discrimination task, the study dissociated developmental components of perceptual decisions: accuracy improved via fewer attention lapses and more efficient evidence accumulation reaching half their change by about 9 years, whereas non-decision time shortened only between 11 and 14 years. Visual response strength did not grow with age, indicating accuracy and speed mature on separate timetables.

papers.title: Cross-modality Knowledge Transfer Between fMRI and EEG for Improved Single-modality Alzheimer's Disease Diagnosis.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) disrupts brain function in both spatial organization and temporal dynamics, which can be characterized by complementary fMRI and EEG measurements. In particular, fMRI provides higher spatial resolution to characterize multi-scale functional organization of brain networks, whereas EEG offers higher temporal resolution to capture dynamic neural activities across frequency bands. Thus, integrating the two modalities can characterize AD-related spatiotemporal disruptions more comprehensively than either modality alone. However, it is impractical to acquire paired fMRI and EEG data in real-world applications. To address this problem, we propose the fMRI-EEG Knowledge Transfer Network (FE-KTNet) to learn spatiotemporal representations from paired data and then transfer them back to modality-specific models through three stages. Specifically, in Stage 1, it learns modality-specific representations from fMRI and EEG FCNs, emphasizing multi-scale network organization for fMRI and frequency-specific electrophysiological coupling for EEG. Building on these representations, in Stage 2, it performs scale-wise bidirectional cross-modality fusion to integrate complementary information into fused multi-scale spatiotemporal representations. Finally, in Stage 3, it transfers the fused representations back to each modality-specific encoder through scale-wise feature alignment and logit-level knowledge distillation. We evaluate FE-KTNet on 14 multicenter datasets comprising 2,766 fMRI subjects and 1,842 EEG subjects, covering AD-NC, MCI-NC, and AD-MCI classifications. Compared with the corresponding baseline models, FE-KTNet increases fMRI-only and EEG-only accuracy by 3.4% and 6.1% for AD-NC classification, 5.2% and 8.0% for MCI-NC classification, and 3.5% and 7.1% for AD-MCI classification, respectively, and achieves the best overall performance among all evaluated methods. Our code is available at GitHub Repository.

papers.title: Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridging Network for Motor Execution to Motor Imagery EEG Transfer in Brain-Computer Interfaces
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery brain-computer interfaces (MI-BCIs) hold promising application prospects in the fields of limb motor rehabilitation and human-computer interaction. However, the reliability of MI calibration data is limited by the difficulty of verifying participants' engagement during motor imagerywhereas motor execution (ME) provides a more readily supervised source of motor-related information.To investigate the potential of ME-derived knowledge for assisting MI decoding, we propose a Shared-Encoder Residual Task-Bridge Network (SE-RTBNet) to achieve accurate intra-subject cross-task knowledge transfer from ME to MI. The proposed framework consists of two major components: a shared encoder and a residual task-bridge module. The shared encoder extracts stable general motor representations from multi-band EEG signals and explores the shared feature patterns underlying ME and MI tasks. The residual task-bridge module is equipped with a performance-aware routing mechanism. It adaptively compensates for task-specific discrepancies between the two tasks, enabling precise cross-task feature alignment and knowledge transfer. To validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, experiments are conducted on three public datasets. The proposed method achieves average classification accuracies of 69.39%, 74.61%, and 98.94%, respectively, and outperforms existing transfer-learning algorithms in overall performance. Our model provides an effective strategy for reducing dependence on extensive MI calibration data through intra-subject cross-task knowledge transfer.The source code of the proposed SE-RTBNet is publicly available at https://github.com/Daisyzyx2002/SE-RTBNet

On three public datasets it achieved average classification accuracies of 69.39%, 74.61%, and 98.94%, outperforming existing transfer-learning algorithms and reducing reliance on MI calibration data.

papers.title: A multimodal dataset for the study of cybersickness under stress and mental workload during immersive VR driving.
papers.abstract: Cybersickness is a common issue in immersive virtual reality (VR), causing symptoms such as nausea, dizziness, and eye strain. In demanding VR training scenarios, stress and mental workload may influence cybersickness severity. However, further research requires datasets that capture these factors alongside subjective and objective measures. This paper presents a multimodal dataset collected during a VR driving simulation to investigate cybersickness in relation to stress and mental workload. Sixty participants completed a phase-based driving task in immersive VR. All participants performed three initial driving phases with progressively increasing difficulty, followed by a condition-specific final phase designed to elicit mental workload, stress, or a combination of both (20 participants per condition). Self-report questionnaires assessing cybersickness, mental workload, and stress-related symptoms were administered at multiple time points during the experiment. Physiological and behavioral data were continuously recorded using an instrumented VR headset and wearable sensors, including electroencephalography (EEG), cardiovascular signals, respiration, and head movement. Representative analyses of subjective and objective measures were conducted to validate the dataset. The analyses demonstrate changes in cybersickness symptoms across driving phases and experimental conditions, illustrating the potential of the collected data to examine cybersickness alongside stress and mental workload. This multimodal dataset provides a resource for neuroergonomics research on cybersickness in immersive VR driving scenarios. By integrating self-reported symptoms with physiological and behavioral measurements, it supports future investigations into the relationships between cybersickness, stress, and mental workload, as well as the development of approaches for monitoring and mitigating cybersickness in demanding VR applications.

ai.summary: Presents a multimodal dataset from 60 participants performing phase-based immersive VR driving tasks, with a final phase designed to elicit mental workload, stress, or both. Records EEG, cardiovascular, respiration, and head-movement data alongside self-report cybersickness, workload, and stress measures, and demonstrates changes in cybersickness symptoms across driving phases and conditions.

papers.title: Evidence for decoder-label-regime-dependent effects of complementary leaky integrate-and-fire temporal-state decoding in motor-imagery EEG.
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery electroencephalography often provides limited subject-specific supervision. This study tested whether complementary leaky integrate-and-fire (CLIF)-family temporal-state decoding shows a decoder-level advantage after the EEG representation is fixed, how that advantage changes with decoder-label availability, and whether hard binary spikes are required. ANN-SEW, the artificial neural network comparator with spike-element-wise (SEW) residual topology, and SEW-CLIF received identical frozen attention-based temporal convolutional network (ATCNet) and filter-bank convolutional network (FBCNet) representations. The evidence chain combined BCI Competition IV Dataset 2a (BCI2a) development, retrospective OpenBMI replication, an internally pre-access-held-out BCI Competition IV Dataset 2b (BCI2b) evaluation, cross-entropy-only label-budget analyses, and a separate internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 Session-A-to-Session-B evaluation. Additional robustness analyses included shared whole-sequence readout for parameter-matched gated recurrent unit (GRU) and temporal convolutional network (TCN) decoders, exact-gradient sigmoid-gated Soft-CLIF, equal optimizer-update budgets, a within-BCI2a binary sensitivity analysis, and computational profiling. Under cross-entropy-only training, SEW-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 10.082 percentage points (pp) on BCI2a and 5.470 pp. on OpenBMI, while full-budget BCI2b remained near parity (+0.181 pp). The ANN-relative gap decreased as decoder labels increased and persisted under equal-update training. At 25 labels/class, exact-gradient Soft-CLIF exceeded ANN-SEW by 11.085, 8.479, and 5.809 pp. on BCI2a, BCI2b, and OpenBMI, respectively. With matched whole-sequence readout, hard SEW-CLIF was broadly comparable to GRU-Stat and TCN-Stat on BCI2a and BCI2b and modestly higher on OpenBMI. The internally pre-access-locked BNCI2015-001 evaluation showed the same attenuation, with a slope of -2.319 pp. per label doubling (95% CI, -4.118 to -0.604). CLIF-family temporal-state dynamics show a reproducible decoder-label-regime effect under frozen supervised representations. Hard forward discretization is not required for the ANN-relative effect, and matched temporal readout substantially reduces differences between CLIF and other continuous temporal decoders.

papers.title: Cognitive capacity in subjective cognitive decline: Insights from electrophysiological markers and dual-task performance.
papers.abstract: Subjective cognitive decline (SCD) refers to self-reported cognitive deficits in the absence of objective cognitive impairment. Evidence suggests that neural changes may precede performance declines, highlighting the potential of electroencephalography (EEG) to detect early cognitive declines. Electrophysiological markers and changes in cognitive and motor performance were examined during dual-task performance to better understand the neural mechanisms underlying SCD. Older adults with (n=20) and without (n=20) SCD performed a working memory and finger tapping task simultaneously (i.e., dual task) and alone (i.e., single cognitive or motor). Linear mixed models were used to assess task and group effects for behavioural performance and EEG measures, including mean amplitude and power spectral density, in frontal, central, and parietal regions of interest (ROI). P2 and P3b mean amplitude were smaller during the dual task compared to single cognitive task. Additionally, the SCD group exhibited higher theta power overall and higher alpha power in each task and ROI compared to the non-SCD group. Higher power was observed during the dual task compared to single tasks except in the alpha band where the opposite was observed. Cognitive and motor performance decreased between single and dual tasks, and slower finger tapping speed was observed in the SCD compared to the non-SCD group. Neural and performance findings support the capacity sharing model of attention and may reflect the use of compensatory mechanisms in the SCD group. Electrophysiological changes may precede objective cognitive deficits and have the potential to complement existing approaches to characterizing SCD but must be examined longitudinally.

papers.title: Cerebellar structural and electrophysiological alterations associated with neuropathic pain in mice.
papers.abstract: The cerebellum is increasingly implicated in pain, yet direct electrophysiology in neuropathy is scarce. We tested whether sciatic nerve chronic constriction injury (CCI) alters cerebellar dynamics and structure. Adult male mice underwent CCI, von Frey testing, structural MRI, spontaneous LFP recordings in lobules IV-V, and spontaneous/evoked single-unit recordings under anesthesia. CCI produced rapid, persistent mechanical hypersensitivity. Deformation-based morphometry (DBM) revealed regional volumetric alterations including localized contractions in the IV-V cerebellar lobules. Spontaneous LFPs showed reduced absolute δ/θ power, with unchanged relative (normalized) power, while β/γ were unchanged. Multi-unit activity in CCI mice exhibited higher firing rates, shorter inter-spike intervals, and larger spike amplitudes. Peripheral stimulation evoked larger responses in CCI. Neuropathic pain is associated with structural remodeling, suppressed spontaneous slow-band cerebellar activity and enhanced unit/evoked responsiveness, which we interpret, as a working hypothesis, as a low-synchrony/high-gain operating regime. These structural and electrophysiological changes are candidate signatures that motivate future mechanistic and causal studies of cerebellar involvement in neuropathic pain.

papers.title: Corticomuscular or electroencephalography-electromyography coherence and intermuscular or electromyography-electromyography coherence.
papers.abstract: The central nervous system and the peripheral effectors must work together to enable accurate and precise movement. Coherence analysis is a mathematical method used to assess the correlation between two recorded signals. In neurophysiology, corticomuscular coherence quantifies functional connectivity between the central nervous system and the peripheral effectors, while intermuscular coherence quantifies the degree of shared neural input to distinct motor units. This chapter begins with an overview of rhythmic activities related to motor control, such as the brain activities measured by electroencephalography or magnetoencephalography, and the muscle activities measured by electromyography. And then, we introduce the fundamental principles of coherence analysis and its computation. Finally, we discuss corticomuscular and intermuscular coherence, highlighting its characteristics and clinical significance, particularly in pathologic conditions. Despite its mathematical simplicity, coherence analysis provides valuable insights into the neurophysiologic mechanisms underlying motor control in healthy conditions and in neurologic disorders.

papers.title: Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method versus CBT-I for Sleep-Onset Chronic Insomnia: A Randomized Controlled Trial Protocol Integrating fMRI and PSG.
papers.abstract: Sleep-onset chronic insomnia is one of the most common sleep disorders in clinical practice and carries a substantial multidimensional burden, including somatic symptoms, emotional distress, and impaired quality of life. Although Prolong Life with Nine Turn-Method has long been used to promote sleep, its specific efficacy for this subtype lacks adequate empirical support. To assess the long-term efficacy and safety of PLWNT in sleep-onset chronic insomnia and to investigate, via multimodal techniques, its modulatory effects on cerebral cortical networks. This prospective, single-center, parallel-group randomized controlled trial will enroll 128 patients with ICSD-3-diagnosed sleep-onset chronic insomnia, randomized 1:1 to a 12-week PLWNT or CBT-I intervention in a superiority design. The primary endpoint is the baseline-to-week-12 change in PSQI total score. Secondary measures include validated scales (ISI, PSAS, HADS, PSS, HAS, MEQ, MFI-20, GSRS, SF-36), sleep diary, actigraphy, blood biomarkers, gut microbiota, PSG, and resting-state fMRI. Exploratory mechanistic endpoints include (1) EEG-derived spectral power and wPLI within the DMN, SN, and CEN during wakefulness, sleep-onset latency, and sleep stages (N1-N3, REM), and (2) resting-state fMRI connectivity of the same networks. Clinical assessments occur at baseline (week 0), week 6, week 12 (end of intervention), and weeks 16, 20, 24, and 36 after randomization (7 time points); laboratory and imaging measures are obtained at baseline and week 12 only. Primary analysis will use generalized estimating equations on LOCF-imputed data, with multiple imputation as a sensitivity analysis. This randomized controlled trial directly compares PLWNT with CBT-I for sleep-onset chronic insomnia, integrating clinical outcome measures with neuroimaging-based mechanistic insights. The findings could position PLWNT as a non-drug therapeutic option backed by objective imaging data.

papers.title: Neural Profiles of Pistol Shooting Performance Across Skill Levels in Hearing and Deaf Shooters: Insights into Cognitive-Motor Processes.
papers.abstract: Precision sport performance requires optimal motor preparation supported by efficient neural processing. While the psychomotor efficiency framework has been used to explain expertise-related neural patterns, it remains unclear whether such neural signatures generalize across individuals with different sensory experiences. The present study aimed to examine expertise-related neural oscillations during motor preparation in 10-m air-pistol shooting by comparing skilled and novice performers in hearing and deaf populations. Study 1 included 37 hearing participants (skilled: n = 19; novice: n = 18), whereas Study 2 included 43 deaf participants (skilled: n = 19; novice: n = 24). Electroencephalography (EEG) was used to assess temporal alpha asymmetry (T4 minus T3), parietal alpha, occipital alpha, frontocentral alpha, sensorimotor rhythm (SMR), and frontal midline theta during the 4 s preceding trigger pull. In Study 1, skilled hearing shooters showed lower temporal alpha asymmetry, reflecting relatively greater left temporal alpha power. They also exhibited higher posterior and frontocentral alpha power, a time-specific increase in SMR, and higher frontal midline theta power relative to novice shooters. In contrast, Study 2 revealed a distinct neural profile in deaf shooters. Deaf novices showed a time-dependent decrease in temporal alpha asymmetry as the trigger pull approached, whereas skilled deaf shooters remained relatively stable. In addition, skilled deaf performers showed reduced frontocentral alpha and SMR power relative to novices, indicating greater sensorimotor cortical engagement during motor preparation. These findings highlight population specificity in expertise-related neural profiles, indicating that neural markers of expertise may not generalize across sensory contexts. Rather than reflecting a universal pattern of psychomotor efficiency, the observed neural profiles may vary across populations with different sensory experiences. Overall, the present study highlights the importance of considering sensory experience when examining neural optimization and provides insights into the cognitive-motor processes underlying skilled performance across diverse athletic populations in precision sports.

papers.title: Data-Driven EEG-fMRI Fusion: From Multimodal Integration to Latent Neural Inference.
papers.abstract: Simultaneous electroencephalography (EEG) and functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) capture neural dynamics across complementary temporal and spatial scales, but analyzing them jointly is difficult: the two modalities differ in measurement mechanisms, temporal resolution, and neurovascular coupling. EEG-fMRI fusion can be framed as an inverse problem, where the goal is to recover latent neural processes only partially observed through electrophysiological and hemodynamic signals. Here, we review data-driven fusion methods published between 2000 and 2025, focusing on techniques that identify shared neural representations across modalities. We organize methods by fusion strategies (symmetric vs. asymmetric), methodological objectives (factorization vs. translation), and modeling assumptions (linear vs. nonlinear), and discuss evaluation metrics and visualization strategies in current use. A recurring finding is the absence of a universal validation standard and the difficulty of interpreting latent multimodal components. Across neurological, psychiatric, and cognitive applications, EEG-fMRI fusion has revealed distributed network dynamics not accessible through unimodal analyses, though temporal misalignment, noise-induced coupling, and model-dependent interpretation remain persistent challenges. We close by discussing directions including nonlinear modeling, flexible coupling frameworks, and large-scale group-level fusion, and situate the field within a broader view of EEG-fMRI fusion as a problem of latent neural inference.

papers.title: Brain-computer interfaces in the motor system: The technologies.
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) translate neural activity into control signals for external devices and neuromodulatory/actuator systems, offering new avenues to restore, rehabilitate, or augment motor function after neurologic injury and disease. The field's foundations lie in early demonstrations that volitional modulation of cortical neurons is possible (operant conditioning), resulting in direct brain-computer interfacing, which catalyzed decades of translational research. Clinical advances now span noninvasive scalp electroencephalography systems that pair sensorimotor rhythms or movement‑related cortical potentials with proprioceptive or functional electrical stimulation (FES) feedback for post‑stroke rehabilitation, to invasive electrocorticography and intracortical arrays enabling multi‑degree‑of‑freedom robotic control and, more recently, limb reanimation through intracortical‑to‑FES neuroprostheses. This chapter critically reviews (i) signal acquisition technologies (noninvasive and invasive), (ii) design considerations for motor BCIs (spatiotemporal resolution, latency, stability, artifacts, and clinical workflow), (iii) signal processing and artificial intelligence approaches for decoding intent, (iv) hybrid systems that integrate neural with peripheral signals such as EMG and inertial sensing, and (v) feedback modalities-from visual and auditory to proprioceptive and state‑dependent stimulation. We conclude with an outlook on minimally invasive implants, wearable sensors, and calibration‑lite artificial intelligence models, and discuss translational milestones and barriers toward routine clinical adoption in neurology and neurosurgery.

papers.title: A Latent Variable Perspective on EEG Measures of Attentional Control
papers.abstract: Attentional control is a core cognitive function, yet there is still a significant debate revolving around its definition, factorial structure and underlying neural mechanisms. Research in this domain has largely developed along two largely disconnected traditions. Psychometric approaches assess individual differences using latent-variable models (e.g., structural equation modeling, confirmatory factor analysis), while cognitive neuroscience focuses on group-level behavioral and neural effects. This raises a critical question: can neural measures robust at the group level validly capture stable individual differences? Or more specifically, can some of the principles and analytical methods adopted in individual-differences research be directly applied to neural correlates of attentional control? The current study aims to address this question. Electroencephalogram data were recorded from participants as they completed four attentional control paradigms: a change detection task, the go/no-go task, the Simon task, and the Stroop task. From each task, we extracted the P3 component and a data-driven decoding accuracy measure as indices of conflict processing and tested whether these neural measures load onto a common latent factor of attentional control. Results revealed weak and largely non-significant correlations. Structural-equation modeling provided no evidence for a common latent factor, despite robust within-task effects at the group level reflected both in the behavioral and the EEG parameters. These findings suggest that EEG components may lack the construct validity needed to reliably capture individual differences in attentional control.

papers.title: Adoption of Routine Intraoperative Raw EEG at a Quaternary Pediatric Centre.
papers.abstract: Intraoperative electroencephalography (EEG) allows real-time assessment of the anesthetic state of the brain and offers a means of titrating anesthetic delivery in children. Randomized trials have shown that EEG-guided titration reduces anesthetic exposure, shortens emergence and recovery, and lowers the incidence of emergence delirium, yet routine use outside research settings has remained largely confined to enthusiastic clinicians and clinical trials. To describe the adoption of routine intraoperative raw EEG monitoring over time at a quaternary pediatric hospital, to characterize practice variation among anesthesia providers, and to identify patient and procedural factors associated with EEG use. We conducted a retrospective single-center study of anesthetic records in the electronic health record from 17 October 2024, when automated EEG capture began, to 30 June 2026, following departmental implementation of routine raw EEG monitoring. Providers were categorized by EEG use as high (> 40% of cases), moderate (20%-40%) or low (< 20%). Trend, provider-level, and procedural associations with EEG use were examined using segmented regression, mixed-effects logistic regression, and clustered logistic regression. Of 26 168 analyzed cases, 21.7% (5674) involved intraoperative EEG monitoring, provided by 59 staff anesthesiologists, 9 senior fellows, 24 fellows, and 102 residents. EEG use rose from 17.8% of cases in October 2024 to 28.4% in June 2026. Use varied widely among staff anesthesiologists (median 18.1%, IQR 12.3%-31.3%; range 0.9%-79.5%); 59.3% (35/59) were low users, and 18.6% (11/59) were high users, with the five highest users accounting for 27.0% of all EEG-monitored cases managed by staff. Case mix explained only a small proportion of this variation (pseudo R2 = 0.064). EEG-monitored cases were more often longer, involved neuromuscular blockade, TIVA maintenance, cardiac surgery, and trainee presence. Adoption of routine raw EEG monitoring increased steadily but nonlinearly following implementation. Variation in use among providers was only weakly explained by case mix, indicating that individual practice patterns, more than patient or procedural characteristics, drove uptake. Efforts to broaden EEG monitoring may benefit from targeting low-use providers and during fellowship training.

papers.title: Commercially available multimodal LLMs for EEG-based prognostication after cardiac arrest.
papers.abstract: Machine-learning and deep-learning approaches have been successfully applied to EEG-based prognostication in comatose patients after cardiac arrest (CA), but typically rely on task-specific signal processing, feature extraction, and model development. Here, we investigated whether two commercially available multimodal large language models (LLMs) could predict neurological outcome directly from EEG images. Thirty-three comatose patients on the first day after CA from a prospective cohort were included. For each patient, a single 10-second EEG segment displayed using a longitudinal bipolar montage was rendered as PNG image. ChatGPT 5.4. and Claude Opus 4.7 were instructed to estimate the probability for favorable outcome for each case based on the EEG and a generic information block describing conditions of recordings. Five different prompting strategies were used, including few-shot prompting where four exemplary EEGs (not from the 33 patients) were provided. Predictive performance was quantified using AUC and accuracy. Across prompting strategies, the AUC ranged from 0.86 to 0.99 for ChatGPT and from 0.74 to 1.00 for Claude. The highest accuracy achieved by both models was 93.9% using few-shot prompting. As reference, a previously published dedicated deep-learning model achieved 100% on the same cohort. In this exploratory study of a small cohort, multimodal LLMs showed variable but potentially promising discrimination for predicting favorable outcome from single EEG image in comatose patients after CA. Performance depended substantially on prompt design. These findings require confirmation in a larger cohort.

papers.title: An Integrated Approach for Early In Vitro Sedation Prediction Utilizing hiPSC Neurons and Human Ion Channel Assays.
papers.abstract: Central nervous system (CNS) liabilities remain a significant cause of failure in drug development. Two complementary in vitro safety assays were previously developed, combining automated patch-clamp electrophysiology and multielectrode array techniques, to detect and avoid seizurogenic compounds. Further to seizure risk, sedation and fatigue are commonly encountered CNS side effects during drug safety testing. Here, the aim was to extend the capability of the in vitro safety assay to enable earlier detection of sedative potential. Fourteen compounds with reported sedative activity and five non-sedative controls were screened in human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived neurons using multielectrode array. These compounds were further screened with automated patch-clamp electrophysiology using cells expressing CNS ion channels implicated in sedation: KV1.1, KV2.1, KV3.1, KV7.2/7.3, NaV1.2, K2P2.1, or the α1β2γ2 GABAA, and α4β2 nicotinic receptors. Known sedative compounds reduced neural firing and network burst activity in human-induced pluripotent stem cell-neurons, indicating sedative effects, whilst negative control compounds did not significantly change multielectrode array parameters. Of the 19 compounds screened, 94% were accurately classified. Automated patch-clamp electrophysiology confirmed that several sedative compounds interacted with CNS ion channels within a 30-fold margin to their total therapeutic blood plasma concentration. These results support the use of the combined in vitro safety models for detecting sedative as well as seizurogenic effects, offering valuable human-based tools for early hazard identification and prioritization of drug candidates. These platforms are also useful for interpretation of CNS-related findings in vivo supporting the principles of 3Rs to minimize and replace the use of animals in scientific testing.

papers.title: ALI MEA60: A porous thin-film microelectrode array for air-liquid interface electrophysiology of 3D excitable tissues
papers.abstract: Objective: Conventional microelectrode arrays (MEAs) are suboptimal for long-term electrophysiology of three-dimensional (3D) excitable tissues, as limited oxygenation, nutrient diffusion, and tissue-electrode coupling compromise recording stability. Air-liquid interface (ALI) culture mitigates these constraints, but existing ALI MEA platforms are limited in channel count, flexibility, and compatibility with commercial multichannel acquisition systems. We developed and comprehensively characterized a next-generation ALI MEA for standardized, long-term recordings across multiple 3D excitable tissue models. Approach: The novel ALI MEA60 is composed of a porous polyimide membrane that integrates an array of 60 thin film microelectrodes (59 recording, one reference) and a basal perfusion chamber with Luer-lock connectors for controlled medium exchange and pharmacological wash-in/wash-out. It is compatible with the MEA2100-Mini data acquisition system (Multi Channel Systems). We characterized electrode impedance and noise across 41 ALI MEA60 devices, assessed 60-day stability with human iPSC-derived neural spheroids (N = 7 MEAs, 121 recordings) using a standardized longitudinal framework and linear mixed-effects models, and evaluated its versatility through pharmacological assays and recordings from human neural spheroids, brain organoids, ex vivo brain slices, and cardiac organoids. Main results: The platform showed reproducible electrical performance (median impedance 56 kOhms; at 1 kHz) and low noise (approx. 5uV Root Mean Square (RMS) in saline, 10-20 uV in medium), resolving spikes and local field potentials simultaneously. Recording remained stable for at least 60 days, with a stable noise floor and ~85% persistence of initial functional channels. Neural spheroids reproduced the standard qualitative signatures to gabazine, 4-aminopyridine (4-AP), and 6-Cyano-7-nitroquinoxaline-2,3-dione/D-2-amino-5-phosphonovalerate (CNQX/D-AP5), while cardiac organoids showed the expected beta-adrenergic response to isoproterenol. The ALI MEA60 can similarly record signals from human brain slices and organoids without hardware modification. Significance: The ALI MEA60 combines ALI culture, chronic recording stability, standardized pharmacological testing and cross-tissue compatibility in a single ready-to-use platform. It also establishes a reproducible framework for benchmarking long-term electrophysiological performance, thereby supporting disease modelling, drug discovery, organ-on-chip technologies and future chronic 3D electrophysiology systems. Keywords: microelectrode array (MEA); air-liquid interface (ALI); 3D excitable tissues; neural spheroids; cardiac organoids; chronic electrophysiology.

papers.title: Electrophysiological correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of pain
papers.abstract: Positive and negative expectations can substantially shape pain and analgesic treatment outcomes, highlighting the need to elucidate neural mechanisms underlying placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia. The primary aim of this feasibility study was to assess adaptations to an established placebo-nocebo conditioning pain paradigm in the context of electroencephalography (EEG). The secondary aim was to assess EEG correlates of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia during the anticipation and delivery of experimental heat pain in healthy volunteers. Placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia were induced in a within-subjects design in 20 young adults through verbal instructions, a conditioning procedure and (sham) transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation while EEG was recorded. Placebo and nocebo effects as well as positive and negative pain expectations were successfully established, demonstrating paradigm effectiveness. EEG results showed increased theta, alpha and beta power in the placebo compared to the control condition during pain delivery, and in the nocebo compared to the control condition during pain anticipation and delivery. Additionally, gamma-band power was increased in the nocebo compared to the placebo condition as a function of a higher perceived pain intensity. Taken together, feasibility of the EEG-compatible placebo-nocebo conditioning pain paradigm was demonstrated. Furthermore, our EEG results are in line with previous findings that, in the context of placebo hypoalgesia and nocebo hyperalgesia, link theta-, alpha- and beta-band activity to top-down processing, and gamma-band activity to expectation-modulated sensory processing.

papers.title: Females with Epilepsy Show Menstrual Cycle-linked Alterations in Sensory Induced Plasticity.
papers.abstract: Catamenial epilepsy describes menstrual cycle-linked exacerbation of seizure frequency and/or intensity. To investigate its neurophysiological mechanisms, we assessed visual long-term potentiation (LTP) across the menstrual cycle using EEG and photic stimulation. Oestradiol can enhance NMDA receptor-mediated excitation and facilitate LTP, whereas allopregnanolone, a progesterone metabolite, promotes GABAergic inhibition and suppresses LTP. We recruited 28 females with epilepsy and 25 controls (mean age: 27 ± 8.52; 30 ± 7.06 years, respectively). Twenty participants with epilepsy and all controls successfully completed the visual LTP task across three menstrual phases: mid-follicular, mid-luteal, and perimenstrual. Cycle phase was verified via blood samples, and session order was counterbalanced. Standard evoked-related potential (ERP) analysis was paired with generative modelling of thalamocortical circuits. In controls, P2 potentiation, a positive-going component of the ERP, was enhanced by LTP induction during the mid-follicular phase compared to the perimenstrual phase (F(2, 144) =11.54, p = 0.004 FWE-c). In contrast, females with epilepsy exhibited greater P2 potentiation during the perimenstrual and mid-luteal phases than the mid-follicular phase (F(2,228) = 11.76, p = .003 FWE-c), with only two participants showing control-like pattern of peak mid-follicular potentiation. Computational modelling indicated loss of inhibitory control and breakthrough excitability during the perimenstrual and mid-luteal phases in epilepsy. Our findings reveal aberrant menstrual cycle modulation of sensory-induced plasticity in epilepsy, suggesting altered inhibitory gating as well as thalamocortical excitatory drive in the mid-luteal and perimenstrual phases. While GABAergic mechanisms are often emphasised in catamenial epilepsy, our results warrant considering altered excitatory mechanisms.

papers.title: Differential effects of α-synuclein aggregates on the electrophysiology of SNpc vs VTA dopaminergic neurons in acute mouse slices.
papers.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterised by the early loss of dopaminergic neurons (DNs) in substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) with other DNs more resistant. Aggregation of alpha synuclein (α-Syn) appears to be a major driver of pathology. We have investigated the differential effects of intracellular α-Syn aggregates on the electrophysiology of SNpc and VTA DNs in acute slices. Introduction of α-Syn aggregates into single SNpc DNs increased whole-cell conductance and altered firing, effects partially reversed by the KATP channel inhibitor glibenclamide. These effects were either absent or much weaker in VTA DNs. Although diazoxide (KATP channel opener) had little effect on VTA DNs compared to SNpc, the effects were significantly enhanced by α-Syn aggregates. These findings demonstrate that acute introduction of α-Syn aggregates significantly changes the electrophysiological properties of SNpc DNs, which is mediated in part by the presence of KATP channels, with these effects much reduced in VTA DNs.

papers.title: Spreading voltage buildup in high density EEG during migraine aura: A longitudinal single-patient study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate spreading features in surface high-density electroencephalogram (HD-EEG) during migraine aura. Approximately 20%-30% of people with migraine experience migraine with aura (MwA). Migraine aura consists of transient neurological deficits such as visual, sensory, speech, motor, brainstem, or retinal symptoms. Clear features of cortical spreading depolarization (CSD) during migraine aura have recently been demonstrated using intracranial depth electrodes in a patient with MwA and comorbid epilepsy; however, in patients with MwA without comorbid epilepsy, direct detection of CSD in a non-invasive setting is still lacking. We report a longitudinal 256-channel HD-EEG study with a direct coupled amplifier set-up in a 45-year-old patient with MwA, in whom repeated recordings could be acquired during aura including early phases and interictally. Electrodes over the forehead, cheeks, periauricular, and nuchal regions were removed to reduce muscle artifacts, resulting in 172 electrodes. In total, 14 electroencephalograms (EEGs) were acquired, thereof eight during the ictal phase. In two out of four aura recordings with predominantly right homonymous scintillating scotoma, recorded soon after onset, we observed a spreading voltage buildup with contralateral maximum. This was associated with a spreading power increase in the delta frequency band. Voltage increases between neighboring electrodes showed a spread with velocity of estimated at 3.8 mm/min. During auras, increased voltage was observed, predominantly in occipital and temporal electrodes. We suggest that topographically related amplitude buildup and delta spread in temporal relation with aura progression reflects CSD. Since invasive CSD detection has been suggested as a useful neuromonitoring tool, with prognostic and therapeutic relevance, further confirmatory studies for non-invasive CSD detections are warranted.

papers.title: Transcranial magnetic stimulation-electroencephalography - relation to motor physiology.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) in combination with transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) opens up the possibility to measure brain responses to TMS. This is a relatively novel technology that significantly extends the longer-established technologies of TMS of the motor cortex (M1) and recording of motor evoked responses via electromyography. TMS-EEG of M1 results in a typical sequence of TMS-evoked responses (TEPs), such as the P30, N45, P60, N100, and P200. TEPs constitute spatiotemporally complex waveforms that arise from both local neuronal activation and recurrent neuronal activity propagated across multiple cortical and subcortical regions. Response components<70 ms are caused by direct TMS effects, while later responses are significantly contaminated by peripherally evoked potentials caused by the auditory and somatosensory inputs from the TMS pulse. P30 reflects local M1 excitability controlled by voltage-gated ion channels, while N45 and P60 reflect excitation-inhibition balance controlled by GABAAergic and glutamatergic neurotransmission. Several recent studies demonstrate the emerging clinical utility of TMS-EEG responses in the diagnosis and outcome prediction of several motor disorders, such as motor stroke and Parkinson disease.

papers.title: Report-derived interictal epileptiform discharge burden is associated with 7-day antiseizure medication decisions after pediatric video electroencephalography.
papers.abstract: To determine whether a three-level interictal epileptiform discharge (IED) burden abstracted from qualitative wording in issued pediatric video electroencephalography (VEEG) reports, rather than directly measured spike frequency, was associated with antiseizure medication (ASM) decisions within 7 days. This single-center retrospective cohort included 216 VEEG report episodes from 181 children. Two reviewers independently classified each report as showing no, low, or moderate-to-high IED burden while unaware of the standardized 7-day outcome; disagreements were adjudicated. We separately analyzed a diagnostic/initiation cohort for new ASM initiation and an established-epilepsy cohort for exploratory treatment intensification. Associations were assessed using exact and trend tests and logistic regression with patient-clustered robust standard errors. Agreement was 211/216 (97.7%); linear-weighted Cohen κ was 0.975 (patient-clustered bootstrap 95% CI 0.947-0.995). The diagnostic/initiation cohort comprised 113 reports from 112 children, with 36 new ASM initiations. Initiation rates were 13.0%, 42.9%, and 70.0% for no, low, and moderate-to-high burden, respectively (trend p < 0.001). The adjusted odds ratio per higher burden grade was 2.89 (95% CI 1.58-5.30; p < 0.001). The established-epilepsy cohort comprised 103 reports from 76 children, with 13 intensification events. Moderate-to-high burden versus none/low yielded an odds ratio of 4.73 (95% CI 1.31-17.08; p = 0.018), but complementary analyses were not statistically significant. Report-derived IED burden showed a strong graded association with new ASM initiation within 7 days. The treatment-intensification finding was exploratory. These data describe prescribing context and do not establish causality, treatment benefit, or an IED-based treatment threshold.

papers.title: Clinical use of transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with electroencephalography in the motor system.
papers.abstract: Transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with electroencephalography (TMS-EEG) has emerged as a powerful technique to investigate cortical physiology and network dynamics in vivo. By directly recording the cortical response to noninvasive brain stimulation, TMS-EEG enables the assessment of cortical inhibitory and excitatory mechanisms, oscillatory activity, and effective connectivity within large-scale network organization independently of the corticospinal output pathways. These properties make TMS-EEG particularly valuable for studying disorders affecting the motor system. This chapter reviews the principles of TMS-EEG in the motor system and summarizes its application in four major neurologic disorders leading to motor network dysfunction, including stroke, amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), Parkinson's disease, and multiple sclerosis. Across these, TMS-EEG has provided novel insights into disease-specific mechanisms, including cortical disinhibition, network reorganization, diaschisis, pathologic oscillatory activity, and alterations in brain complexity. Furthermore, growing evidence suggests that TMS-EEG-derived measures are associated with clinically relevant outcomes such as motor impairment, recovery potential, disease progression, and treatment response. Although methodologic challenges and the need for larger and longitudinal cohorts remain, TMS-EEG represents a promising approach for characterizing network dysfunction and may contribute to future treatment strategies in neurology.

papers.title: Surgical outcomes in stereoelectroencephalography versus subdural grids: a systematic review & meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Invasive extra-operative monitoring for drug-resistant epilepsy is primarily conducted using stereo-electroencephalography (SEEG) and subdural grids (SDG). This study aims to provide a comprehensive comparison of the two methods. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA guidelines. A comprehensive literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Database. The primary outcomes assessed included postoperative seizure outcome, complications, neurological deficits, and pain. All original English-language studies published up until January 2025 were reviewed, and the risk of bias was evaluated using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Seven studies involving a total of 1,156 patients who underwent SEEG and 737 patients who underwent SDG were included. The pooled analysis demonstrated higher odds of seizure freedom in the SEEG group compared with the SDG group (OR = 1.72, 95% CI: 1.33-2.22). However, the included studies compared clinically distinct patient populations with different indications for invasive monitoring and surgical pathways, which may have influenced seizure outcomes. Across the included studies, SEEG was consistently associated with lower infection rates and reduced postoperative analgesic requirements, while rates of hemorrhage and neurological deficits were generally comparable between groups, with some studies reporting slightly higher hemorrhage rates in SEEG cohorts. SEEG was associated with higher odds of seizure freedom following epilepsy surgery; however, this finding should be interpreted with caution because the included studies compared clinically distinct patient populations with different indications for invasive monitoring, surgical pathways, and resection rates. The available evidence suggests lower infection rates and reduced postoperative analgesic requirements with SEEG, whereas findings regarding hemorrhage and neurological deficits were variable across studies. Further studies with larger, more comparable patient populations are needed to better define procedure-specific risks and outcomes.

papers.title: Validation of drug-resistant epilepsy identification algorithms in US Veterans across diverse care settings.
papers.abstract: Early recognition of drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) is critical for timely referral to comprehensive epilepsy centers (CECs). Our prior pilot study in the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) demonstrated the feasibility of an algorithm-based approach to identify DRE within selected CECs. In this study, we validated and refined these algorithms in a broader, national cohort, including CEC and non-CEC care, to optimize algorithms for different care settings. We conducted a multicenter, retrospective study of randomly sampled veterans with epilepsy on ≥2 antiseizure medications (ASMs) from 1999 to 2024. Chart review by 26 epilepsy providers rated DRE status. Ninety-six candidate algorithms using combinations of six criteria-number of ASMs, treatment duration, dose thresholds, pregabalin exclusion, intractable International Classification of Diseases (ICD) codes, and electroencephalography (EEG)/magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) utilization-were evaluated. Performance for DRE classification was evaluated among all veterans, and separately for CEC or non-CEC care. Among 970 veterans on ≥2 lifetime ASMs, 518 (53.4%) were rated as DRE, 363 (37.4%) as non-DRE, and 89 (9.2%) as undetermined. Veterans with DRE were younger (mean age = 68.9 vs. 72.0 years) and more frequently had at least one intractable ICD code (46.1% vs. 18.2%), EEG (77.8% vs. 66.7%), or MRI (78.0% vs. 65.8%) compared with non-DRE (all p-values <.001). Among all veterans, the best overall algorithm (area under the curve [AUC] = .701) identified DRE as either (1) exposure to 3+ ASMs or (2) exposure to two ASMs for at least 1 year, with the requirement of past EEG/MRI and intractable ICD code documentation. This algorithm was also highly effective among veterans who received CEC (AUC = .756) or only non-CEC care (AUC = .678). This national validation study confirms that medication-based algorithms can identify DRE within VHA administrative data across care settings (CECs and non-CECs). This supports the implementation of a standardized DRE definition for quality improvement, surveillance, and referral optimization within the VHA.

papers.title: Influenza A-Associated Encephalitis and Encephalopathy in Adults: An Exploratory Criteria-Based Analysis.
papers.abstract: Influenza A can cause encephalopathy or encephalitis, yet adult data are scarce and the two entities are seldom distinguished systematically. This small retrospective study of five adults explored the feasibility and limitations of classifying these complications with the International Encephalitis Consortium (IEC) 2013 criteria and describes their clinical, radiological, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), and treatment characteristics. We retrospectively reviewed five consecutive adults admitted to a tertiary center with polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-confirmed influenza A and acute neurological symptoms, all evaluated with brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), lumbar puncture, and electroencephalography (EEG). Encephalitis was defined by the IEC 2013 criteria (altered mental status > 24 h plus ≥ 2 minor criteria of central nervous system (CNS) inflammation). Data were analyzed descriptively. Three patients met criteria for encephalitis and two for encephalopathy (four women; age 44-68 years). Respiratory influenza A PCR was positive and CSF PCR negative in all. CSF pleocytosis occurred in two patients, bilateral thalamic and subcortical white matter MRI hyperintensities in two, generalized EEG slowing in four, and focal status epilepticus in one. All received oseltamivir; three received high-dose methylprednisolone, two of whom also required intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange. The categories overlapped substantially: EEG slowing and negative CSF PCR occurred in both, and treatment escalation followed clinical course rather than category, with the most intensive regimen required by one patient in each. At 3 months, three patients were asymptomatic and two, both with encephalitis and structural MRI lesions, had persistent deficits. In this small, hypothesis-generating study, IEC-based classification was feasible, but encephalitis and encephalopathy overlapped substantially and the distinction did not determine treatment. The main contribution lies in illustrating both the feasibility and limitations of criteria-based classification in adults with influenza A, rather than in establishing its clinical utility.

papers.title: De novo POLR2A p.(L1127F) variant presenting with neurodevelopmental regression and dystonia, with favorable response to low-dose dopamine therapy: a case report and literature review.
papers.abstract: Neurodevelopmental disorder with hypotonia and variable intellectual and behavioral abnormalities (NEDHIB) is a rare autosomal-dominant condition caused by pathogenic POLR2A variants. It typically presents in infancy with hypotonia, developmental delay, and multisystem manifestations. Fewer than 40 patients have been reported worldwide, suggesting frequent misdiagnosis and underdiagnosis. To our knowledge, neurodevelopmental regression has not been documented in confirmed NEDHIB cases, and no standardized therapeutic regimens are established for clinical management. The patient presented with neonatal hypotonia and developmental delay. At 2 years and 4 months, she developed sleep-associated dystonia-like nodding and limb tremors that were initially suspected to represent epileptic seizures. By 3 years of age, she exhibited marked neurodevelopmental regression: loss of the ability to walk and sit independently, together with deterioration of language function. Electroencephalography (EEG) demonstrated background slowing accompanied by epileptiform discharges. Whole-exome sequencing identified a de novo heterozygous POLR2A variant c.3379C > T (p. L1127F), which confirmed the diagnosis of NEDHIB. Long-term rehabilitation training yielded only modest clinical benefits. After initiation of the dopamine agent levodopa-benserazide hydrochloride, marked improvements in motor and cognitive performance were observed, accompanied by the complete resolution of nodding episodes. With dose titration during follow-up, her clinical status remained stable without symptom relapse. This case expands the phenotypic spectrum associated with POLR2A-related NEDHIB and suggests that neurodevelopmental regression may occur within the phenotypic spectrum of this disorder. Our findings also highlight the potential benefit of low-dose dopamine therapy, offering novel insights into the clinical diagnosis, differential diagnosis, and therapeutic management of NEDHIB.

papers.title: Coal Tar-Based Driveway Sealant Extract Induces Mutations in Liver, Bone Marrow, and Germ Cells of MutaMouse Male Mice.
papers.abstract: Coal tar-based driveway sealants (CTS) are a widespread but underrecognized source of human exposure to mutagenic polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs). We used Duplex Sequencing, an error-corrected sequencing technology, to assess the mutagenicity of a complex PAH mixture extracted from a CTS in MutaMouse male mice. We observed significant dose-dependent increases in mutation frequency (MF) in liver and bone marrow, with mutation spectra dominated by C:G > A:T substitutions, closely resembling a mutational signature linked to human cancers associated with tobacco smoking. In germ cells, we did not observe a statistically significant increase in MF, although there was a positive dose-response trend and enrichment of C:G > A:T mutations at higher doses. The mutagenic effects of CTS in germ cells were supported by a statistically significant increase in mutant frequency measured using the plaque-based lacZ assay. Tissue-specific analyses revealed greater mutation susceptibility and potency in liver, likely reflecting its central role in PAH metabolism. Mutation spectrum analysis showed that the mutagenic profile of the CTS extract largely resembled that of benzo(a)pyrene; however, detailed spectral analysis indicated additional contributions from other PAHs or PAH metabolites that produced distinct mutational patterns. Collectively, our findings demonstrate that the CTS extract induces tissue-specific mutagenic responses driven by characteristic C:G > A:T mutations, offering mechanistic insight into how environmental PAH mixtures contribute to mutation burden and cancer risk.
